findings.issue: Nothing binds a work list's jobs to a specific snapshot, and nothing records which snapshot a running list used. `newest_snapshot()` picks whatever has the newest `.deploy_complete`, `resolve_snapshot` only checks that the tree is complete and has `worker_pool.sh`, and the items file / job name / `--wrap` line carry no SHA. The campaign deliberately runs the SAME item list in two lanes (`p0_mlp_mig` + `p0_mlp_a100_overflow`, likewise P1/P3), which are necessarily two separate invocations of this tool, and CONTRACTS.md requires a re-deploy after every commit. `grid.run_hash` (experiments/experiment_code/grid.py:764-815) hashes the resolved `dataset`, `model`, `num_epochs`, `loss` and `_HASH_EVAL_KEYS` (`eval_batch_size`, `eval_every_steps`, `train_eval_size`), so two snapshots whose configs differ in any of those give every run of the scan a different hash8 -- and the C-R3 rule is then "a marker with another hash8 => move that run's jsonl/npz/ckpt/marker to _stale/ and run". This is not hypothetical: while I was reviewing, the configs track changed the CIFAR and kappa configs under me (cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression went 510 -> 555 runs, cifar10_resnet_ce_scan 570 -> 655, mnist_kappaScan_labelRegression 150 -> 210).
findings.suggested_fix: Stamp the resolved snapshot path + both full SHAs into the items-file header, the job name/log and DEPLOY_INFO echo; before submitting a list, `squeue`-check for queued/running jobs whose name matches this list (or whose items file is the same path) and refuse unless their recorded snapshot is identical (or `--force` is given). Also print the snapshot's sv3/sven SHAs next to the live HEADs so a mismatch is visible in the dry run.
findings.failure_scenario: Launch `--phase P0 --lane mig` from snapshot A. The configs track then adds `train_eval_size` to mnist_scan_ce; the orchestrator commits and re-deploys, producing snapshot B. Launch `--phase P0 --lane a100` -- `newest_snapshot()` returns B. Both job sets now walk mnist_scan_ce mode=svd. Every run finished by the A jobs has marker hash8_A; the B workers see a marker under another hash, move the finished jsonl/npz/ckpt to `_stale/hash8_A/` and re-run it, writing hash8_B; the A workers do the same in reverse. 640 Sven runs ping-pong between the two lanes for the life of both jobs, and every completed record ends up in `_stale/`.

findings.issue: `--chain` can never renew in the one situation it exists for. `chain_script` emits no `--signal=B:...` and installs no trap, and `worker_pool.sh` has no wall-clock budget (grep: the only `trap` is worker_pool.sh:201, no `--signal`, no deadline anywhere). At the 12 h gpu_test limit Slurm SIGTERMs every process of the job, including the batch shell; bash's default SIGTERM disposition terminates it, so the `rc=$?` / reconcile / `sbatch` renewal block after the `worker_pool.sh` call at line 259 is never reached. The pool only exits on its own when every item's claim queue is drained -- i.e. exactly when reconcile would say "nothing left" and the chain would not renew. So `--chain` is strictly worse than the plan's default (`n_jobs: 2`): it turns two 12 h MIG jobs into one, and the promised self-renewal never fires. I confirmed the bash behaviour directly (a foreground-child shell SIGTERMed mid-command never printed the line after the child).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `#SBATCH --signal=B:USR1@900` to the chain script plus `trap 'touch "$STOP"' USR1` wiring that asks the pool to stop starting items and returns control to the renew block; or give `worker_pool.sh` a `WORKER_TIME_BUDGET`/`--until` (from `$SLURM_JOB_END_TIME` or the lane's `-t`) so it stops starting new items ~15 min before the wall and exits 0. Until one of those exists, drop `chain: true` from the plan's notes and the `--chain` recommendation in the plan header, or say plainly that renewal only happens if the list drains early.
findings.failure_scenario: `tools/launch_campaign.py campaign/plan_campaign.yaml --phase P1 --lane mig --chain --submit`. The p1_mlp list is 71 items / ~2000+ MIG-hours of work, so the job is still running at 12 h. Slurm sends SIGTERM; worker_pool exits 143 and the batch shell dies with it. No `[chain]` line is ever logged, no renewal is submitted, and the MIG lane (~2.5 A100-equivalents at a measured 3 s queue wait) sits idle until a human notices -- overnight that is roughly a GPU-day.

findings.issue: Both tools compose the LIVE `experiments/configs` (`--config-dir` default None -> `reconcile.ConfigLoader` -> REPO/experiments/configs, reconcile.py:139-142) while the jobs they describe run the snapshot's configs. The dry-run run counts, the `optimizers_standard` warnings, reconcile's expected grid, its never-started list and its grid-edge report therefore describe a config the workers are not running. Demonstrated live during this review: the same `--phase P0` selection reported 510/570 runs for the two CIFAR scans at one point and 555/655 twenty minutes later, purely from another track's edits, while the snapshot on disk (`sv3_deploy/6fd8fd9e_203a4e61`) still holds the pre-Stage-1 configs.
findings.suggested_fix: Default `--config-dir` to `<snapshot>/experiments/configs` whenever a snapshot is resolved (fall back to the repo with a printed note when none is), and have reconcile accept/derive the snapshot the same way (or print the config dir it used next to each scan, as it already prints the results dir).
findings.failure_scenario: The snapshot's `mnist_scan_ce` has `train_eval_size: 10000`; the configs track then sets it to 5000 in the live tree. A human runs `tools/reconcile.py --all campaign/plan_campaign.yaml --phase P0`: every finished run's hash8 computed from the live config differs from the marker written by the workers, so all 1360 runs are reported `stale-hash` and the exit code is 1 -- "work remains" for a scan that is complete. Acting on that (relaunching, or letting a chain renew) re-runs the whole scan and retires the finished results to `_stale/`.

findings.issue: The MIG cap check is `existing + want > lane.max_jobs`, which permits filling the partition completely with chained jobs -- contradicting the module docstring's explicit promise: "This tool therefore refuses to submit a chain that would leave no free slot (1 chained job + at most 1 other)". Verified by running `--phase P0,P1 --lane mig --chain --no-count`: it prints `lane cap mig: 0 queued + 2 wanted <= 2 OK` and two `$ sbatch ....chain.sbatch` lines. Two chains occupy both MaxSubmitPU slots, so neither can ever renew into a free slot; the chain script's 10x60 s `sbatch` retry loop just fails ten times and gives up. (Three chains are correctly refused, which is what makes the two-chain case look sanctioned.)
findings.suggested_fix: When any planned job for a capped lane is a chain, require `existing + want < lane.max_jobs` (i.e. leave one slot free) and say so in the refusal message; alternatively allow at most one chain per capped lane and force the rest of the selection to plain jobs.

findings.issue: `resolve_root` ignores the plan's `results_root` even in the `--all <plan>` path: the root is `--root`, else `$SV3_RESULTS_ROOT`, else `REPO/experiment_results`. The plan carries `results_root: /n/holystore01/.../sven_experiments` (plan_campaign.yaml:31) and `tools/launch_campaign.py` exports exactly that to the workers, so reconcile and the launcher can disagree about which root they are talking about. Today the three paths coincide, but campaign/CAMPAIGN_STATUS.md line 76 instructs people to work with `SV3_RESULTS_ROOT=../experiment_results_legacy_2026-09-18` exported, and the plan's own header advertises the bare command `tools/reconcile.py --all campaign/plan_campaign.yaml --phase P0`.
findings.suggested_fix: In `main`, when `a.plan` is given and `--root` is not, prefer `plan.results_root` over `$SV3_RESULTS_ROOT` (or at least warn when the two differ), and print the root once in the header alongside the per-scan `dir` line.
findings.failure_scenario: In a shell where `SV3_RESULTS_ROOT` points at the frozen legacy root, `tools/reconcile.py --all campaign/plan_campaign.yaml --phase P0` reconciles the fresh campaign plan against the read-only 2026-09-18 legacy results: the 734 legacy toy_1d records have no `done/` markers at all, so everything comes back `jsonl-only`/`never-started`, exit 1, and the operator concludes the P0 scans have not run.

findings.issue: `best_configs` gates eligibility on the METHOD being in the expected grid (`b["in_grid"] = method in methods_expected`, line 410) but never on the CONFIGURATION. For a config_key absent from `expected`, `n_exp` falls back to `g["n"]` (the number of records found), so `config_eligible(1, 1)` is True and a single off-grid record can be reported as a method's best config with `in_grid: True`; because its value is not in `options`, the edge check for that axis is silently skipped, so the operator sees no verdict for it rather than a warning. The plan's P2 stub says the extension items are filled "from tools/reconcile.py <scan>" and the timing section says reconcile "prints the per-method best config the selection needs", so this feeds both C-B3 and the phase-5 selection. Reproduced: with a finished 15-run tiny scan plus one stray `svd_..._lr0.9_...` record at 1e-9, reconcile reports best SVD = `lr 0.9, k 4`, `n_ok/n_expected = 1/1`, `edges = {k: EDGE-HIGH}`, `in_grid = True`. (Related, lower: HIG's `tau` is never edge-checked although grid_counts.md records tau as an axis C-B3 extends, so a HIG best sitting at the top tau is reported as interior.)
findings.suggested_fix: Skip records whose `config_key(run_id)` is not in `expected` when building `groups` (or keep them but mark the entry `in_grid: False` and refuse to let them win), and make a missing/unmatched axis value print an explicit `lr:OFF-GRID` rather than nothing. Add `tau` to the reported axes for the hig family.
findings.failure_scenario: grid_counts.md records that HIG's lr grid was shifted down rather than grown, so the previously-run top lrs are no longer in the config. Once a scan has run under the old grid, those records remain on disk as `unexpected_jsonl`. The next reconcile picks one of them (1 seed, possibly the luckiest) as HIG's best config with no lr edge verdict, and the P2 extension round extends the wrong axis -- or the timing pass times a configuration the campaign never ran.

findings.issue: Per-process logs and hydra run dirs default into the home filesystem: `WORKER_LOG_ROOT=/n/home11/sambt/iaifi/sv3/slurm_logs/campaign` (and `launch_campaign.DEFAULT_LOG_DIR` at launch_campaign.py:49 puts the sbatch `-o` files there too), while every other campaign artefact -- snapshot, work-items files, chain scripts, results -- lives on holystore. `/n/home11` is at 84% with 17 GB free (`df`: 95G size, 79G used), existing `slurm_logs/` is already 181 MB with single shard logs up to 841 KB, and this design multiplies file count: one log per (job x pool x item x NPROC) plus a 3-file hydra dir each, i.e. of order 13,000 logs + 39,000 hydra files for the full plan (P1 alone: 2 jobs x 4 slices x 71 items x 6 = 3408 per lane). A full home makes the `> "$log"` redirect fail and the runner die, and home is NFS, which is the wrong place for thousands of concurrent small appends.
findings.suggested_fix: Default `WORKER_LOG_ROOT` and `--log-dir` under `/n/holystore01/LABS/iaifi_lab/Users/sambt/sv3_campaign_scratch/logs` (the launcher already uses that tree for work items), keeping the env override. While there: export `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` in the pool -- as written, every job writes `__pycache__` into the snapshot the pool's own comments declare immutable.
findings.failure_scenario: Mid-campaign, P0 + P1 jobs on both lanes fill the remaining 17 GB of home with runner logs and hydra dirs. Subsequent `> "$log"` redirections fail, the `( ... exec python )` subshells exit non-zero before doing any work, `worker_pool.sh` reports "N failed runner process(es)" and exits 1 for every remaining item, and the jobs burn their wall clock producing nothing -- while looking like a training failure rather than a disk-full failure.

findings.issue: The track's headline coverage test asserts the plan against another track's markdown, so it fails on an edit that does not touch the plan at all. It fails right now: `AssertionError: plan vs grid_counts.md (plan, table): {'cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression': (555, 510), 'cifar10_resnet_ce_scan': (655, 570), 'mnist_kappaScan_labelRegression': (210, 150)}` (`1 failed, 29 passed` in tests/test_tools_launch.py), i.e. the implementer's reported `68 passed` was already stale when the report was written. The substantive property is fine -- I checked the plan's enabled-item union against each config's OWN full grid (mode=all, no optimizer override, same n_data values) family by family and the only differences are the deliberately parked CIFAR jd/hig (20+80 each) and the ablation configs' incidental `standard` grids, exactly as grid_counts.md documents -- so the failure is indistinguishable from a real coverage loss and will train the operator to ignore it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the coverage assertion intrinsic: for each scan, compare the plan's enabled-item union of (family, run_id) against `expand_grid(compose(scan, 'mode=all' [+ each n_data]))`, allowing only an explicit, commented exclusion list (CIFAR jd/hig, the Sven-only ablation configs, Fig-5). Keep the grid_counts.md comparison as a separate test whose failure message says "grid_counts.md is stale", not "the plan lost runs".

findings.issue: The final `grand_total` double-counts every list that shares items, because the MIG list and its A100 overflow deliberately carry the same items against the same claim queue. `--phase P0` prints `11220 run(s) of grid in scope` where the phase contains 6350 distinct runs (reconcile's own total for the same selection). The coverage test already dedups by `(scan, overrides)`; the operator-facing number does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Accumulate `grand_total` over items deduplicated by `(item.scan, item.overrides)` and keep the per-list subtotal as-is, or label the total "item-runs (lists sharing items counted once per list)".

findings.issue: `repo_facts` calls `die` on a git failure, but it is invoked inside a command substitution (`read -r SV3_SHA ... <<<"$(repo_facts "$REPO")"`), so `exit 1` ends only the subshell. The script has no `set -e`, so it continues with empty SHAs: `SNAP=$BASE/_`, `"git_sha": ""` in DEPLOY_INFO.json, and the `[ "$SV3_DIRTY_TRACKED" = true ]` guard reads as clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture into a variable and check the status explicitly (`out=$(repo_facts "$REPO") || exit 1`), or validate the parsed SHA (`case $SV3_SHA in [0-9a-f]*) ;; *) die ...;; esac`) before building the snapshot name.

findings.issue: `--time` is applied by `_override_time` after the sbatch line has been printed, so with `--submit --time` the command shown is not the command submitted. It is also silently ignored for chained jobs, whose wall clock is baked into the `#SBATCH -t` of the generated script from the lane/list value.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the time override when building `cmd` (before the print), and pass it into `chain_script` so `#SBATCH -t` honours it -- or reject `--time` together with `--chain`.

tests_run:
Ran the track's own suites with /n/home11/sambt/iaifi/sv3/.venv/bin/python -m pytest:

1. First pass, all three files: `68 passed in 22.69s` (tests/test_tools_launch.py, tests/test_tools_reconcile.py, tests/test_tools_worker_pool.py) -- reproduces the implementer's claim.
2. Re-run of tests/test_tools_launch.py ~20 min later, after the configs track edited experiments/configs in the shared tree: `1 failed, 29 passed in 10.14s`. The failure is test_the_plan_covers_every_run_grid_counts_says_exists: `plan vs grid_counts.md (plan, table): {'cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression': (555, 510), 'cifar10_resnet_ce_scan': (655, 570), 'mnist_kappaScan_labelRegression': (210, 150)}` (finding 8).

Independent verification I ran myself (scratchpad scripts, no SLURM jobs submitted, nothing written to any results root):
* Plan-vs-config coverage, family by family: summed expand_grid over the plan's enabled items (deduped by (config, overrides)) and compared with campaign/grid_counts.md -- exact match on all 21 launched scans for every family (svd/standard/lbfgs/polyak/jd/hig), 15545 runs + the 408 parked finetune runs = the documented 15953. No duplicated run_ids across items and no run_id carrying two different run hashes.
* Plan union vs each config's OWN full grid (`mode=all`, plus every n_data the plan passes): the only gaps are CIFAR jd(20)+hig(80) per scan (parked in p3_cifar_jd_hig, documented as out of scope in grid_counts.md) and the Sven-only ablation configs' unused `standard` grids -- re-checked after the live config edits and still clean.
* CUT scans (critbatch x2, gpt2, the four 1-seed CIFAR kappa/paramFrac, mnist_scan_brier) appear nowhere in the plan; no `weight_decays` override anywhere; MNIST overparam n_data tops out at 50000 and matches the config's documented sweep exactly; no `*_timing` config in any work item.
* Dry runs: `--phase P0` (14 jobs printed, 0 warnings), `--phase P0,P1,P3 --lane mig --chain` (correctly refused at 3 chains), `--phase P0,P1 --lane mig --chain` (wrongly allowed at 2 -- finding 4). Confirmed the only submit path is guarded by `if a.submit` and the only other subprocess call is read-only `squeue`.
* `tools/reconcile.py --all campaign/plan_campaign.yaml --phase P0 --no-best`: 7 scans in 3.5 s, exit 1, torch never imported (checked sys.modules), 1.0 s for a single scan.
* Reconciled the reconcile re-implementations against the originals: config_key regex, is_diverged, final_value, config_eligible vs analysis/style.py; CLAIM_SUFFIX/`.claim.N` generations, STARTED_SUFFIX, CLAIM_TIMEOUT_S=600, DONE_STATUSES and the `rsplit('.', 2)` marker format vs experiments/experiment_code/claims.py -- all consistent. Records do carry top-level `lr`/`k`/`rtol`/`batch_size`/`optimizer` and are written with mode 'w', so reading line 1 is correct.
* Built a synthetic finished scan with one off-grid stray record: reconcile reports it as the best SVD config with `n_ok/n_expected = 1/1`, `in_grid: True` and no lr edge verdict (finding 6).
* Checked nvidia-smi -L captures from the GPU probe (`probe_results/env/mig_3g20gb/gpu_list.txt`, a `--gres=gpu:2` job listing exactly 2 MIG devices): Slurm does constrain devices on gpu_test, so the pool's MIG discovery and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES index mapping are correct. hydra is 1.3.4, so `hydra.job.chdir` defaults to False and the pool's cwd=snapshot reasoning holds.
* Demonstrated that a batch shell SIGTERMed while a foreground child runs never reaches the following lines (finding 2).
* Confirmed no SLURM jobs were submitted by this track (squeue: one unrelated `interactive`; today's sacct shows only `devtest` CPU test jobs from campaign/run_cpu_tests.sh), the fresh results root is still empty, the legacy root is still read-only and untouched (mtime 2026-09-17), and `tools/check_token_split.py` is unmodified.
